title: Disruptions in circadian rhythms and nicotinamide metabolism caused by chemoradiotherapy are associated with behavioral toxicities in esophageal cancer
description: This study aimed to explore the systemic molecular mechanisms underlying behavioral toxicities, particularly sleep disturbance, in patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) undergoing definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy (dCRT). We performed a prospective, single-center, paired longitudinal study including 30 ESCC patients, with peripheral blood samples collected before treatment (T0) and after treatment (T1). We integrated mRNA-seq transcriptomics and plasma untargeted metabolomics, combined with patient-reported symptom assessments using the MDASI-GI-C scale. Multivariate statistical and multi-omics network analyses were applied to identify key genes, metabolites, and biological pathways associated with treatment-induced symptom worsening. The results revealed that dCRT leads to significant downregulation of core circadian rhythm genes and disruptions in nicotinate/nicotinamide metabolism and retinol metabolism, which are closely linked to exacerbated sleep disturbance and other behavioral toxicities. This transcriptomic dataset provides a comprehensive resource for understanding the systemic molecular alterations underlying chemoradiotherapy-related toxicities in esophageal cancer and supports the development of potential biomarkers and intervention targets.
